harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent CentOS 5-compatible host firewall on node1. IPv4 and IPv6 now permit loopback, established traffic, ICMP, SSH/TCP 22, and TCP 8080, then explicitly reject other inbound traffic. The original OS release and kernel remain unchanged. Persistence was proven through a successful node restart.
actions_performed: Backed up the original iptables and ip6tables configurations.
Installed no new software; used the existing legacy iptables 1.3.5 stack.
Enabled iptables and ip6tables for runlevels 2–5.
Verified SSH remained operational after applying the rules.
Safely restarted node1 once and verified its boot identity changed.
Confirmed SSH, firewall services, saved rules, and runtime rules recovered after restart.

evidence.requirement: Persistent firewall permits SSH and TCP 8080 and rejects unrelated inbound traffic
evidence.summary: Validated saved IPv4/IPv6 configurations, successful firewall reload, boot enablement, live rules for TCP 22 and 8080, terminal REJECT rules, and post-restart recovery.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged; the existing iptables-1.3.5 package was used.

Captured healthy baseline with boot ID 7fb5e2ce-1b6b-4465-8000-000000000000, received restart acknowledgement, then observed changed boot ID edb24c1e-1abc-4add-8000-000000000000 with SSH listening and both firewall policies restored.
